title: The Italian Game
blurb: The oldest opening in chess. Quick development, and the bishop points straight at Black's weakest square.

lines.label: Giuoco Piano
lines.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Greco Gambit, Traditional Line
ideas: Claim the centre and open lines for the bishop and queen.
Develop with a threat — the knight already eyes e5.
The Italian bishop. It stares at f7, the square only the king defends.
Quiet but purposeful: c3 prepares to build the big centre with d4.
Now the centre breaks open while you are the better developed side.
Recapture toward the centre. You have pawns on d4 and e4 — the ideal pair.
Block the check and offer a trade. Your centre survives intact.

lines.label: Giuoco Pianissimo
lines.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Giuoco Pianissimo
ideas: Claim the centre.
Develop and attack e5.
The Italian bishop takes aim at f7.
The 'very quiet game'. Support e4 and keep every piece defended.
Prepare d4 at leisure. There is no hurry in a closed position.
Castle first, decide on a plan second.

lines.label: Two Knights Defense
lines.name: Italian Game: Two Knights Defense, Polerio Defense, Bishop Check Line
ideas: Claim the centre.
Develop and attack e5.
The bishop eyes f7.
Crude but strong: two pieces now hit f7 and Black must react.
Take the pawn and keep the extra material for now.
Check, and hang on to the pawn a little longer.
Grab it. Black gets fast development for the pawn — play carefully.

lines.label: Evans Gambit
lines.name: Italian Game: Evans Gambit, Pierce Defense
ideas: Claim the centre.
Develop and attack e5.
The bishop eyes f7.
A pawn for time. Deflect the bishop so you can build the centre with tempo.
Hit the bishop again and prepare d4 — every move comes with a threat.
Cash the gambit in: a huge centre while Black is still untangling.
Castle. Down a pawn, but far ahead in development and with open lines.
